tasks.title: Rung 2: Open and close the scissors using only the holding hand's digits.
tasks.description: The robot must open and close the scissors using only the digits of the hand that is holding the handles, simulating the natural human action of using the fingers through both loops. The robot must maintain a stable grip on the handles while performing the opening and closing motion.
success_measures: The robot must achieve a minimum of 5 full open/close cycles.
The opening and closing motion must be achieved solely by the digits of the holding hand, without external pushing or mechanical assistance.
The simulation must confirm that the pivot movement is driven by the digits of the holding hand, not by the wrist or forearm.
capabilities_needed: Fine motor control and dexterity in the holding hand's digits.
Ability to isolate and control the movement of the digits relative to the object's pivot point.

tasks.finding: Vertical digits through horizontal loops cannot hold a pair whose halves turn freely on the pivot: any digit pressing a loop's wall swings the half out of its way (the halves sit ~10 deg from their stops), and a lift catches nothing. A person's scissors hang on HORIZONTAL digits, gravity on the digits, the loops' planes vertical.
tasks.next: Insert vertically, squeeze the loops to the blades' closed stop (both halves pinned against each other), lift 1-2 cm on that squeeze, turn the hand so the digits are horizontal and the pair hangs on them (the wrist roll about the spread line), ease the squeeze, then cycle the thumb's spread. Or pick the pair from a vertical presentation (hung by its blades), entering the loops horizontally.

tasks.title: Rung 3: Setting the Forward/Reverse Switch
tasks.description: The robot must set the forward/reverse switch (located on the handle) using a finger (e.g., middle or ring finger) and then pull the trigger to demonstrate controlled speed and direction.
success_measures: The robot must successfully manipulate the switch (e.g., from 'off' to 'forward') and maintain contact force on the switch for a minimum of 1 second.
The robot must then pull the trigger (trigger_peak_fraction >= 0.8) to demonstrate maximum speed control, resulting in a run_rpm of at least 700 RPM.
capabilities_needed: Fine motor control to manipulate a small, discrete switch (Rung 3).
Coordination to combine switch setting and trigger pulling in sequence.

tasks.title: Thread a digit round a handle: plan the arm and the hand's joints together against the tool's exact surface
tasks.description: A person's pistol grip closes the thumb round the handle's back. For the R5's Ability Hand on drill_1 that grip exists, but every way to it passes through the handle: a palm-fixed thumb sweep is blocked (two islands of clear thumb configurations), and a straight slide with the thumb already wrapped drives it through. The hand must come round the handle while the thumb opens and closes - a path in the arm's 8 joints and the thumb's 2 at once, collision-checked against the tool's surface (slab hulls), not its bounding box, which is what the reach checker uses now.
success_measures: the critic's thumb_opposes passes on the drill: the thumb flexed >= 0.4 rad, pressing the handle >= 1 N
no tool contact before the grip's close (the take's contact log)
capabilities_needed: an RRT or trajectory optimiser over arm + hand joints with the tool's hulls as obstacles
the hand's contact geometry (HomeHero collision cache) in that checker

tasks.title: Robot posture joint states use an unregistered schema name
tasks.description: build_er_scene authors the robot's posture with apiSchemas 'PhysxJointStateAPI:<kind>'; the PhysX schema registers the joint state as 'PhysicsJointStateAPI' (omni.usd.schema.physx plugInfo: schemaIdentifier PhysicsJointStateAPI). The object joint_state path uses the registered name and PhysX applies it (the scissors' halves start at +8.6/-7.0 deg in the articulation view). So every robot scene starts at the zero pose and its drives pull the arms to the posture in the settle. Fix the name, then re-run each robot scene's settle and compare its first-second contacts.
success_measures: the articulation view's dof positions at the first physics step equal the posture (within 1e-3 rad)
the scenes' grasp verdicts unchanged or better
